def parse_csv(text: str, delimiter: str = ",") -> list[list[str]]:
    """Parse CSV text into rows of fields without using the csv module."""
    if not text:
        return []

    rows: list[list[str]] = []
    # Split into lines on \n or \r\n (a lone \r is not a line break here).
    lines = []
    i, n = 0, len(text)
    while i < n:
        j = i
        while j < n and not (
            text[j] == "\n"
            or (text[j] == "\r" and j + 1 < n and text[j + 1] == "\n")
        ):
            j += 1
        lines.append(text[i:j])
        if j < n:
            i = j + 2 if text[j] == "\r" else j + 1
        else:
            i = n
    # A trailing line terminator does not create a new record.
    if lines and lines[-1] == "":
        lines.pop()

    for line in lines:
        rows.append(_parse_line(line, delimiter))
    return rows


def _parse_line(line: str, delimiter: str) -> list[str]:
    fields: list[str] = []
    buf: list[str] = []
    i, n = 0, len(line)
    dlen = len(delimiter)
    while i < n:
        ch = line[i]
        if ch == '"':
            # Quoted field: starts here.
            i += 1
            closed = False
            while i < n:
                c = line[i]
                if c == '"':
                    if i + 1 < n and line[i + 1] == '"':
                        buf.append('"')
                        i += 2
                        continue
                    closed = True
                    i += 1
                    break
                if c == "\n" or (c == "\r" and (i + 1 >= n or True)):
                    # Embedded newline inside quotes: treat as content.
                    buf.append(c)
                    i += 1
                    continue
                buf.append(c)
                i += 1
            if not closed:
                raise ValueError("Unterminated quoted field")
            # After the closing quote only a delimiter, end-of-line, or
            # (in this implementation) embedded content is allowed.
            if i < n and not line.startswith(delimiter, i):
                raise ValueError(
                    "Invalid character after closing quote in field"
                )
            if i < n:
                i += dlen
            fields.append("".join(buf))
            buf = []
        elif line.startswith(delimiter, i):
            fields.append("".join(buf))
            buf = []
            i += dlen
        else:
            buf.append(ch)
            i += 1
    fields.append("".join(buf))
    return fields

def parse_csv(text: str, delimiter: str = ",") -> list[list[str]]:
    """Parse CSV text into rows of fields, without using the csv module.

    Records are separated by \\n or \\r\\n. A single line terminator at the
    end of the text does not create a new record. A field that starts with
    a double quote may contain the delimiter, line breaks and "" (which is
    taken as a single " inside the field); quotes are not part of the field.
    """
    if not text:
        return []

    n = len(text)
    dlen = len(delimiter)
    rows: list[list[str]] = []
    fields: list[str] = []
    buf: list[str] = []
    i = 0

    def close_field() -> None:
        fields.append("".join(buf))
        buf.clear()

    def close_record() -> None:
        close_field()
        rows.append(fields)
        fields = []

    while i < n:
        ch = text[i]

        if ch == '"':
            # Quoted field: read until the closing quote.
            i += 1
            closed = False
            while i < n:
                c = text[i]
                if c == '"':
                    if i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == '"':
                        buf.append('"')
                        i += 2
                        continue
                    closed = True
                    i += 1
                    break
                # A line break inside quotes is content of the field.
                if c == "\n":
                    buf.append("\n")
                    i += 1
                    continue
                if c == "\r":
                    if i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == "\n":
                        buf.append("\r\n")
                        i += 2
                    else:
                        buf.append("\r")
                        i += 1
                    continue
                buf.append(c)
                i += 1
            if not closed:
                raise ValueError("Unterminated quoted field")
            # After the closing quote: delimiter or end of record only.
            if i < n and not text.startswith(delimiter, i):
                nxt = text[i]
                if nxt in ("\n", "\r"):
                    close_record()
                    i += 2 if (nxt == "\r" and i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == "\n") else 1
                    continue
                raise ValueError(
                    "Invalid character after closing quote in field"
                )
            if i < n:
                i += dlen
            fields.append("".join(buf))
            buf = []

        elif text.startswith(delimiter, i):
            close_field()
            i += dlen

        elif ch == "\n" or (ch == "\r" and i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == "\n"):
            close_record()
            i += 2 if ch == "\r" else 1

        elif ch == "\r":
            # Lone \r acts as a line break as well.
            close_record()
            i += 1

        else:
            buf.append(ch)
            i += 1

    # Final record (a trailing line terminator already closed it).
    if fields or buf:
        rows.append(fields + ["".join(buf)])
    return rows

    line breaks and "" (taken as a single " inside the field); the
    surrounding quotes are not part of the field. Unquoted fields are
    taken verbatim (spaces preserved); a " in the middle of an unquoted
    field is an ordinary character.

    A ValueError is raised if a closing quote is immediately followed by
    something other than a delimiter or a line break, or if a quote is
    never closed.
    """
    if not text:
        return []

    n = len(text)
    dlen = len(delimiter)
    rows: list[list[str]] = []
    fields: list[str] = []
    buf: list[str] = []
    i = 0

    while i < n:
        ch = text[i]

        if ch == '"':
            # Quoted field: read until the closing quote.
            i += 1
            closed = False
            while i < n:
                c = text[i]
                if c == '"':
                    if i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == '"':
                        buf.append('"')
                        i += 2
                        continue
                    closed = True
                    i += 1
                    break
                # Line breaks inside quotes are content of the field.
                if c == "\n":
                    buf.append("\n")
                    i += 1
                elif c == "\r":
                    if i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == "\n":
                        buf.append("\r\n")
                        i += 2
                    else:
                        buf.append("\r")
                        i += 1
                else:
                    buf.append(c)
                    i += 1
            if not closed:
                # Quote closed at end of line is still unterminated.
                raise ValueError("Unterminated quoted field")
            # After the closing quote: delimiter or end of record only.
            if i < n:
                nxt = text[i]
                if nxt == "\n":
                    fields.append("".join(buf))
                    rows.append(fields)
                    fields = []
                    buf = []
                    i += 1
                    continue
                if nxt == "\r" and (i + 1 >= n or text[i + 1] == "\n"):
                    fields.append("".join(buf))
                    rows.append(fields)
                    fields = []
                    buf = []
                    i += 2 if (i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == "\n") else 1
                    continue
                if not text.startswith(delimiter, i):
                    raise ValueError(
                        "Invalid character after closing quote in field"
                    )
            if i < n:
                i += dlen
            fields.append("".join(buf))
            buf = []

        elif text.startswith(delimiter, i):
            fields.append("".join(buf))
            buf = []
            i += dlen

        elif ch == "\n":
            fields.append("".join(buf))
            rows.append(fields)
            fields = []
            buf = []
            i += 1

        elif ch == "\r":
            fields.append("".join(buf))
            rows.append(fields)
            fields = []
            buf = []
            i += 2 if (i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == "\n") else 1

        else:
            buf.append(ch)
            i += 1

    # Final record (a trailing line terminator already closed the last one).
    if fields or buf:
        rows.append(fields + ["".join(buf)])
    return rows

{"content":"def parse_csv(text: str, delimiter: str = ",") -> list[list[str]]:
    """Parse CSV text into rows of fields, without using the csv module.

    Records are separated by line breaks (\\n or \\r\\n). A single line
    terminator at the end of the text does not create a new record.
    A field that starts with a double quote may contain the delimiter,
    line breaks and "" (taken as a single " inside the field); the
    surrounding quotes are not part of the field. Unquoted fields are
    taken verbatim (spaces preserved); a " in the middle of an unquoted
    field is an ordinary character.

    A ValueError is raised if a closing quote is immediately followed by
    something other than a delimiter or a line break, or if a quote is
    never closed.
    """
    if not text:
        return []

    n = len(text)
    dlen = len(delimiter)
    rows: list[list[str]] = []
    fields: list[str] = []
    buf: list[str] = []
    i = 0

    while i < n:
        ch = text[i]

        if ch == '"':
            # Quoted field: read until the closing quote.
            i += 1
            closed = False
            while i < n:
                c = text[i]
                if c == '"':
                    if i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == '"':
                        buf.append('"')
                        i += 2
                        continue
                    closed = True
                    i += 1
                    break
                # Line breaks inside quotes are content of the field.
                if c == "\n":
                    buf.append("\n")
                    i += 1
                elif c == "\r":
                    if i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == "\n":
                        buf.append("\r\n")
                        i += 2
                    else:
                        buf.append("\r")
                        i += 1
                else:
                    buf.append(c)
                    i += 1
            if not closed:
                # Quote closed at end of line is still unterminated.
                raise ValueError("Unterminated quoted field")
            # After the closing quote: delimiter or end of record only.
            if i < n:
                nxt = text[i]
                if nxt == "\n":
                    fields.append("".join(buf))
                    rows.append(fields)
                    fields = []
                    buf = []
                    i += 1
                    continue
                if nxt == "\r" and (i + 1 >= n or text[i + 1] == "\n"):
                    fields.append("".join(buf))
                    rows.append(fields)
                    fields = []
                    buf = []
                    i += 2 if (i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == "\n") else 1
                    continue
                if not text.startswith(delimiter, i):
                    raise ValueError(
                        "Invalid character after closing quote in field"
                    )
            if i < n:
                i += dlen
            fields.append("".join(buf))
            buf = []

        elif text.startswith(delimiter, i):
            fields.append("".join(buf))
            buf = []
            i += dlen

        elif ch == "\n":
            fields.append("".join(buf))
            rows.append(fields)
            fields = []
            buf = []
            i += 1

        elif ch == "\r":
            fields.append("".join(buf))
            rows.append(fields)
            fields = []
            buf = []
            i += 2 if (i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == "\n") else 1

        else:
            buf.append(ch)
            i += 1

    # Final record (a trailing line terminator already closed the last one).
    if fields or buf:
        rows.append(fields + ["".join(buf)])
    return rows
","path":"csvparse.py"}
